justifications.c1: Independent per-incident fines on food firms are sourced: Ole & Steen £26k fine + £8.8k costs (search-confirmed), a cake maker £60k, Pearl Food £12k, and £16k. The stated pain, independents losing food-site contracts, has no money figure: contract value was not found, and one council's contracts start at £275/yr.
justifications.c2: Food-site contracts run 8, 12 or 24 visits a year by risk level (PPC/BPCA, search-confirmed), with corroboration from Brent (8–14 visits a year) and Abate (12 a year). Every station is checked on each routine visit, at least monthly on medium- and high-risk sites.
justifications.c3: This is a documented, paid, recurring technician service with sourced frequency (PPC, Brent, Abate). The BPCA advises pricing per visit, but the only cost figure is Brent's low-end £275/yr, and the BPCA cautions that sensors should not replace visits.
justifications.c4: BRCGS Issue 9 clause 4.14 (12 sub-clauses: device maps, inspection frequency, annual assessment) is cited only through a Rentokil Poland vendor summary and a consultancy page. Enforcement exists: council prosecutions (Enfield, Westminster/Ole & Steen, Central Bedfordshire) and an IFSQN thread on a 4.14 major non-conformance. No rule requires electronic monitoring, so the idea's premise is unverified.
justifications.c5: The buyer is an independent pest-control firm (the BPCA says 96% of members are SMEs; IBISWorld counts 838 businesses). Owner-operators are plausible buyers, but no title or budget evidence was found, and the food-site technical manager is not evidenced either.
justifications.c6: Distributors already sell connected rodent monitoring to independents for food sites: Pelsis/Edialux (TrapMe, EverSmart), Pestfix (TrapMe £94.64, search-confirmed) and Syngenta SecureChoice via the NPTA and BPCA. The pest controller visits each site 8–24 times a year.
justifications.c7: Crowded, and the stated gap is largely closed: Rentokil PestConnect, Anticimex SMART, Syngenta SecureChoice (retrofits any existing station, sold to independents), Pelsis TrapMe and EverSmart, and TrapSensor. No complaints were found showing independents lack options.
justifications.c8: Retrofit station sensors are commercially proven (SecureChoice, with a 9-year battery claimed). Generic LoRaWAN nodes cost €57–€80, above £50, and gateway and LTE-M backhaul prices were not found. US11602144 creates a freedom-to-operate risk.
justifications.c9: BRCGS annual assessments and contracts with 8–24 visits a year give records a structural, ongoing use, and subscriptions are the norm (TrapMe CAMRO subscription). The visible price anchor is low: the TrapSensor 12-month data plan is about £26/yr inc VAT, roughly £2/month.
justifications.c10: Council enforcement (Enfield, Central Bedfordshire), trade press (Food Manufacture, The Caterer, BPCA) and food-safety forum threads (IFSQN) all exist, but they show infestation and audit pain. The idea's actual pain (independents losing contracts to digital offers) was searched for and not found.

weakest: The claimed gap does not exist: Syngenta SecureChoice retrofits any existing bait station and is marketed to independents through the NPTA and BPCA, and Pelsis/Edialux and Pestfix already sell connected traps to them.
